standard.title: Measure angles with protractor
standard.description: Estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees, using appropriate tools including a protractor, and relate these measures to angle names
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify and name angle types (acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex) (AC9M4M04). They have not yet measured angles in degrees or used a protractor to construct angles.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees using a protractor, and relate measures to angle names.

nodes.label: Degrees as a unit
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that angles are measured in degrees and relate benchmark angles (90°, 180°, 360°) to angle names.
nodes.minimum_width: State that a full turn = 360°, half turn = 180°, quarter turn = 90°; match these to right, straight and full angle names.
nodes.typical_width: Relate all named angle types to degree ranges; use benchmark angles to estimate whether an angle is acute, obtuse or reflex before measuring.
wider: Investigate why 360° was chosen as the unit for a full turn — historical and astronomical context
Connect to clock face: how many degrees does the minute hand turn in one hour?
success_criteria: Student states benchmark angle measures in degrees
Student matches a degree range to an angle name

nodes.label: Estimating angles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can estimate angles in degrees using benchmark angles as reference points.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate an angle to the nearest 10° using benchmark angle knowledge; compare estimate to a measured value.
nodes.typical_width: Estimate a range of acute, obtuse and reflex angles; develop estimation strategies based on benchmark subdivision.
wider: Use estimation in practical design tasks: estimating roof pitch, ramp angle
Investigate how First Nations architecture and design involves angular reasoning
success_criteria: Student estimates an angle within ±15° of actual value
Student uses a named benchmark angle to justify their estimate

nodes.label: Measuring with a protractor
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can correctly position and read a protractor to measure angles, including obtuse angles.
nodes.minimum_width: Measure an acute angle using a protractor, selecting the correct scale; record the measurement in degrees.
nodes.typical_width: Measure acute and obtuse angles using a protractor; identify and use the correct inner/outer scale; verify measurements against estimate.
wider: Measure angles in polygons and verify angle sum properties
Investigate digital tools (dynamic geometry software) as alternatives to physical protractors

response_modes.reason: Protractor use has specific procedural requirements (correct scale, vertex alignment, zero-line placement) where errors cluster. Targeted practice with deliberate attention to each step reduces systematic error.

Students commonly use the wrong scale (read 60° as 120°). Angles in varied orientations and obtuse angles require actively choosing the correct scale — multiple examples with differing angle sizes resolve this.

nodes.hinge_reason: Correct protractor technique — specifically scale selection — is the prerequisite for Node 4 (construction). Students who read the wrong scale construct angles that are consistently wrong by the supplement amount.
success_criteria: Student positions the protractor correctly on an angle
Student reads the correct scale and records the angle in degrees

nodes.label: Constructing angles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a given angle in degrees using a protractor.
nodes.minimum_width: Construct a given acute angle using a protractor; verify by measuring the constructed angle.
nodes.typical_width: Construct acute and obtuse angles; apply to shape construction tasks; check construction accuracy using measurement.
wider: Construct specific angles in geometric patterns or designs
Use dynamic geometry software to construct and verify angles
success_criteria: Student constructs a specified angle within ±2° accuracy
Student verifies the constructed angle by measuring
